examples.question_text: State the horizontal and vertical component vectors of (a) $\underset{\sim}{a}=\begin{pmatrix}-5\\7\end{pmatrix}$ and (b) $\underset{\sim}{b}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\-6\end{pmatrix}$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The top entry gives the horizontal component and the bottom entry gives the vertical component.
$\underset{\sim}{a}=-5\underset{\sim}{i}+7\underset{\sim}{j}$.
The horizontal component vector is $-5\underset{\sim}{i}$; the vertical component vector is $7\underset{\sim}{j}$.

(b) $\underset{\sim}{b}=0\underset{\sim}{i}-6\underset{\sim}{j}$.
The horizontal component vector is $0\underset{\sim}{i}=\underset{\sim}{0}$; the vertical component vector is $-6\underset{\sim}{j}$.

The top entry multiplies $\underset{\sim}{i}$ and the bottom entry multiplies $\underset{\sim}{j}$. Keep both signs.
$\begin{pmatrix}-\frac{7}{3}\\\frac{5}{2}\end{pmatrix}=-\frac{7}{3}\underset{\sim}{i}+\frac{5}{2}\underset{\sim}{j}$.

Read the coefficient of $\underset{\sim}{i}$ first, even though its term is written second. The horizontal component is $\frac{5}{6}$ and the vertical component is $-\frac{9}{4}$.
$-\frac{9}{4}\underset{\sim}{j}+\frac{5}{6}\underset{\sim}{i}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{5}{6}\\-\frac{9}{4}\end{pmatrix}$.

The diagram has editable black labels and semantic component colours, with derived annotations confined to the solution. No bare opening expressions require phantom equals gutters. examples.derivation: The column entries give horizontal and vertical coefficients respectively. For a, these are -5 and 7, giving -5i and 7j. For b, these are 0 and -6, giving the zero horizontal vector and -6j vertically. This follows the Basis Vectors teaching at lines 1863–1891.

Copying the top entry to the coefficient of i and the bottom entry to the coefficient of j gives -(7/3)i+(5/2)j. Both values and signs are preserved. The conversion follows lines 1895–1902; fractional values introduce no additional method.

The coefficient of i is 5/6 and the coefficient of j is -9/4, so the column vector has entries 5/6 above -9/4. Written term order does not change component order. This matches the reversed-order conversion task at lines 1904–1906.

The arrow starts at (5,4) and ends at (1,1), giving horizontal displacement 1-5=-4 and vertical displacement 1-4=-3. Hence v=-4i-3j. The solution component arrows connect (5,4) to (1,4) to (1,1), with correct directions, labels and right-angle marker. The 7 mm grid step matches both coordinate scales. Attached images 20, 21 and 26–31 support decomposition, signed grid reading and geometric-to-component conversion.
